name: New York
overview: New York offers a small refundable low-income owner/renter credit and separate Basic/Enhanced STAR school-property-tax relief.

programs.name: Real Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: All ages; higher schedule if claimant, spouse or a claimed dependent is 65+.
programs.incomeDefinition: Federal adjusted gross income starting in tax year 2025, replacing the prior household-income basis.
programs.maximumBenefit: 2025: up to $75 under age 65, or $375 under the senior schedule.
programs.formulaSummary: Starting in 2025, the credit uses fixed federal-AGI tiers and the age schedule. Renters count 25% of adjusted rent as property taxes; IT-214 line 18 must be greater than zero to claim the credit.
programs.application: IT-214 with IT-201, or standalone IT-214 if no income return is otherwise required.
eligibilityNotes: Full-year resident, same residence at least six months, not claimable as a dependent.
All owned real-property market value must not exceed $85,000.
Qualifying renters face a $450 average-monthly occupancy-rent ceiling.
Residence must not be fully property-tax exempt.
IT-214 line 18 must exceed zero; a zero or negative amount does not qualify.

programs.name: Basic and Enhanced STAR Credit
programs.ageRule: Basic has no age restriction; Enhanced generally requires age 65+, with spouse/sibling and survivor exceptions.
programs.incomeDefinition: STAR income generally equals FAGI minus taxable IRA distributions; 2025 benefits use 2023 income.
programs.incomeLimits: 2025 Basic credit income limit $500,000; Enhanced income limit $107,300. Legacy Basic exemption limit $250,000.
programs.maximumBenefit: Location-specific school-tax savings; no uniform statewide dollar credit.
programs.formulaSummary: New York pays Basic or Enhanced STAR by check or direct deposit using location-specific school-tax savings and qualifying-tax limits. The legacy STAR exemption reduces the bill separately; recipients cannot combine the two delivery forms.
programs.application: Register for the STAR credit; existing exemption recipients follow separate rules.
eligibilityNotes: 2025 Basic uses resident owners and their spouses; Enhanced includes all owners, including nonresident owners, plus resident spouses.
2025 Enhanced generally requires every owner to be 65 by December 31, with specified married-couple, sibling and survivor exceptions. The relaxed 2026 rule is separate.
The September 15, 2025 Tax Department bulletin sets the 2025 ownership and primary-residence date at the last day to pay local school taxes without penalty.
Each joint return contributes STAR income once. STAR income subtracts taxable IRA distributions included in federal AGI, not all pensions, gross IRA withdrawals or Social Security.
interactions: Cannot receive STAR credit and STAR exemption on the same property for the same associated fiscal year. Basic and Enhanced are alternatives.
Eligibility, exemption savings, cash advances and recoveries follow separate rules. An exemption already reflected in a net property-tax bill does not also provide the same credit as cash income.
programs.programYear: 2025 benefit year uses 2023 income; property/school-district facts are necessary.

laterChanges: For 2026 Enhanced STAR, the income limit becomes $110,750 and owner-income eligibility rules change. The 2025 benefit rules use their separate income limits and ownership conditions.
researchNotes: IT-229 is discontinued and does not provide an additional 2025 benefit.
Local senior and disability exemptions depend on local adoption and are not enumerated here.

STAR credit and legacy exemption have distinct income limits, ownership histories, qualifying dates and local amount tables. School-district segments, partial payments and advance recoveries require separate property and payment details.
